text:
May Flower like a ray
of afternoon was dying…
I loved you, May Flower,
you know it; but God did not will it!


Waves come, waves go,
singing they come, singing they will go.


May Flower neither dresses
nor adorns nor arrays herself;
May Flower is very sad!
Poor little thing, poor life of mine!


Each star that pulses,
from heaven speaks to her thus:
“Come with me, little flower,
you will shine in the vastness just like me.”


May Flower, faintly,
answers: “Soon I will go!”


May Flower is dying,
May Flower, the chosen one, has gone from us!


Waves come, waves go,
singing they come, weeping they will go…


“Do not leave me!” I cry to her:
“Do not go, my mistress,
the space is infinite
and very black and cold, so cold!”


Heedless of my pleading,
May Flower moved away,
and in the night, like a dream,
mysteriously sad, was lost.


Waves come, waves go,
singing they come, ah, how will they go!


Under the shelter of my garden
only one flower grew:
May Flower, and she has died…
I loved her, but God did not will it!

translation.title: The May Flower Song
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the refrain, personified flower, and the tension between the speaker’s love and divine will.
